sources.title: Java SE 21 HotSpot Garbage Collector Implementation
Java SE 8 HotSpot GC Tuning Guide Introduction
Java SE 9 java launcher: -Xlog unified JVM logging
Mark-sweep, compact, and copy space model

claims.text: Java SE 21 HotSpot defines garbage as memory for objects no longer reachable from live references, and explains generational collection using the weak generational hypothesis that most objects survive only briefly.

The Java SE 21 HotSpot guide describes Eden and two Survivor spaces, copying surviving young objects between Survivor spaces and promoting them by age or space conditions; young collections primarily process the young generation and their cost is related to live objects collected.

The Java SE 21 HotSpot guide treats throughput, latency, footprint, and promptness as GC tradeoffs and notes that young-generation sizing trades throughput against footprint, promptness, and pause times.

The executable model demonstrates the algorithmic distinction that sweeping can leave non-contiguous holes that cannot satisfy a two-slot contiguous allocation, while compacting or copying surviving objects leaves a contiguous free region; Oracle's Java SE 8 HotSpot guide documents recovery by compacting live objects through parallel copying as a collector implementation mechanism.

JEP 158 was delivered in JDK 9 and introduced the JVM unified logging -Xlog option; the Java SE 9 java launcher documents -Xlog and -Xlog:gc, while the Java SE 21 HotSpot GC guide documents -Xlog:gc* for detailed GC logging and -verbose:gc as an alias for -Xlog:gc. The candidate therefore bounds this syntax to JDK 9+ HotSpot rather than applying it to JDK 8 and earlier.
